title: A General Dihedral Recognition Engine — the missing DihedralGroup.lift
description: A child iteration of `inverse-galois-d4-oq-03` (which proves the specific case Gal(X⁴ − 2 / ℚ) ≅ D₄ by a Sylow argument special to n = 4). The parent's route does not generalise; the general Schinzel–Velez dihedral criterion for X^n − a is blocked upstream on Capelli's irreducibility theorem, absent from Mathlib v4.26.0. This entry supplies the reusable, Capelli-free, **field-theory-independent** group-theoretic core that every dihedral-binomial case needs, filling a concrete Mathlib gap flagged by the parent's audit: there is **no `DihedralGroup.lift`** (presentation-by-generators-and-relations constructor). Two deliverables, both fully machine-verified with 0 sorries / 0 axioms / 0 `native_decide`: (1) `liftHom` — the canonical group homomorphism `DihedralGroup n →* G` induced by a generator pair σ, τ satisfying σⁿ = 1, τ² = 1, τσ = σ⁻¹τ, with the homomorphism law proved *from the relations* (so it works for an arbitrary carrier G, not just a finite S_k, and is not a `decide`); and (2) `nonempty_mulEquiv_dihedralGroup` — the **recognition theorem**: if σ, τ additionally generate a finite G and |G| = 2n (n ≥ 2) then G ≃* DihedralGroup n. This is the n-uniform replacement for the parent's Sylow argument: instead of embedding into S_k and invoking Sylow, one exhibits two generators with the dihedral relations and matches orders.

meta.author: Lean Genius Research
meta.assumptions: 0 axioms, 0 sorries, 0 `native_decide` — fully machine-verified, only Mathlib group theory (no field theory, no `decide`). The homomorphism law of `liftHom` is proved purely from the three dihedral relations σⁿ = 1, τ² = 1, τσ = σ⁻¹τ, so it holds for an *arbitrary* carrier group G (not merely a finite permutation group where `decide` would be available). The recognition theorem `nonempty_mulEquiv_dihedralGroup` adds only the finiteness hypothesis `[Finite G]`, generation `Subgroup.closure {σ, τ} = ⊤`, and the cardinality hypothesis `Nat.card G = 2 * n` (with n ≥ 2); no assumption is structure-encoded. Imports: Mathlib (single umbrella import). Uses `DihedralGroup` and its multiplication simp lemmas (`r_mul_r`, `r_mul_sr`, `sr_mul_r`, `sr_mul_sr`), `DihedralGroup.card`, `ZMod.val_*`, `MulEquiv.ofBijective`, and `Fintype.bijective_iff_surjective_and_card`.
originalContributions: liftHom: the missing `DihedralGroup.lift` — the canonical homomorphism `DihedralGroup n →* G` induced by generators σ, τ : G satisfying the dihedral relations σⁿ = 1, τ² = 1, τσ = σ⁻¹τ. Sends the abstract rotation `r 1` to σ and the abstract reflection `sr 0` to τ. `map_mul'` is discharged by the four DihedralGroup multiplication cases (r·r, r·sr, sr·r, sr·sr), each reduced to periodicity + the single reflection commutation identity — NOT a finite `decide`, so it applies to any carrier group G. This is the reusable constructor Mathlib v4.26.0 lacks.

nonempty_mulEquiv_dihedralGroup: the general dihedral RECOGNITION theorem — a finite group G generated by σ, τ with the dihedral relations and |G| = 2n (n ≥ 2) satisfies G ≃* DihedralGroup n. This is the n-uniform replacement for the parent oq-03's n=4-specific Sylow argument (`order_eight_iso_dihedralFour`): once a Galois group Gal(X^n − a / ℚ) is exhibited with such generators and the right order, this theorem identifies it as D_n with no further group-theoretic work.
liftFun: the underlying set map `DihedralGroup n → G`, rotation `r i ↦ σ^i.val`, reflection `sr i ↦ τ · σ^i.val`, over which `liftHom` is built.
pow_mod: σ-powers are periodic with period n once σⁿ = 1 — `σ^(k % n) = σ^k`. The bridge making `i ↦ σ^i.val` well-defined modulo n.
spow_add: the rotation map is additive — `σ^(i+j).val = σ^i.val · σ^j.val` for i, j : ZMod n (uses `ZMod.val_add` + `pow_mod`).
spow_neg: the rotation map sends negation to inversion — `(σ^i.val)⁻¹ = σ^(-i).val`.
sigma_pow_mul_tau: the iterated reflection–rotation commutation law `σ^m · τ = τ · (σ^m)⁻¹`, proved by induction on m from the single relation τσ = σ⁻¹τ. The engine behind `map_mul'`.
rot_mul_refl: rotation-times-reflection combination law `σ^i.val · (τ · σ^j.val) = τ · σ^(j-i).val`.
refl_mul_refl: reflection-times-reflection combination law `(τ · σ^i.val) · (τ · σ^j.val) = σ^(j-i).val` — where the two reflections cancel via τ² = 1.

liftHom_r_one / liftHom_sr_zero: the two `@[simp]` normalization lemmas identifying `liftHom (r 1) = σ` and `liftHom (sr 0) = τ`, used to prove surjectivity of `liftHom` on the generating set in the recognition theorem.

`Fintype.card (DihedralGroup n) = 2 * n` for `[NeZero n]`; supplies the codomain-cardinality match used to upgrade surjectivity to bijectivity.

overview.historicalContext: Every finite dihedral group D_n admits the classical Coxeter/Dyck presentation ⟨s, t | sⁿ = t² = (st)² = 1⟩ — equivalently, a rotation s of order n and a reflection t of order 2 with t inverting the rotation, tst⁻¹ = s⁻¹. Recognising an abstract group as dihedral from such a generating pair is a routine move in classical group theory and a recurring subgoal in Galois-theoretic formalisation, where a Galois group is first realised concretely (as permutations of roots, or as a metacyclic quotient) and must then be identified up to isomorphism with D_n. Mathlib v4.26.0 provides `DihedralGroup n`, its full multiplication table, its cardinality `2n`, and order witnesses for the generators — but it provides **no constructor building a homomorphism OUT of `DihedralGroup n` from a generator pair satisfying the relations**, i.e. no `DihedralGroup.lift`. The parent open question `inverse-galois-d4-oq-03` discharged its flagship instance Gal(X⁴ − 2 / ℚ) ≅ D₄ by a Sylow argument keyed to |S₄| = 24 (an order-8 subgroup is a Sylow 2-subgroup, all conjugate), a route intrinsically special to n = 4. The uniform Schinzel–Velez criterion for arbitrary (n, a) — the classical answer of Velez (1979) and Schinzel (2000) — is blocked in Lean only by the absence of Capelli's irreducibility theorem (Capelli 1897) from Mathlib. This entry isolates the part of the problem that is provable *now*: the pure group-theoretic recognition engine, entirely independent of field theory and of Capelli.
overview.problemStatement: **Deliverable (inverse-galois-d4-oq-03-incomplete-01)**: supply the reusable group-theoretic core of the general dihedral-binomial problem — a constructor building `G ≃* DihedralGroup n` from a generating pair (σ, τ) satisfying σⁿ = 1, τ² = 1, τστ⁻¹ = σ⁻¹ together with |G| = 2n, and the underlying homomorphism `DihedralGroup n →* G`, both with 0 sorries and 0 axioms.
overview.text: Two theorems and their supporting lemmas, all field-theory-free. `liftHom : DihedralGroup n →* G` is the missing `DihedralGroup.lift`: given σ, τ : G with the dihedral relations it sends `r i ↦ σ^i.val` and `sr i ↦ τ·σ^i.val`, with `map_mul'` proved from the relations (not by `decide`). `nonempty_mulEquiv_dihedralGroup` is the recognition theorem: adding `[Finite G]`, generation `closure {σ, τ} = ⊤`, and `Nat.card G = 2n` (n ≥ 2) yields `G ≃* DihedralGroup n`.
overview.proofStrategy:
Build the homomorphism OUT of `DihedralGroup n` and upgrade it to an isomorphism by matching orders.

1. **Rotation half (well-definedness mod n).** Because σⁿ = 1, the power σ^k depends only on k mod n (`pow_mod`). Packaging `i ↦ σ^i.val` as a ZMod n → G map, the additivity `σ^(i+j).val = σ^i.val·σ^j.val` (`spow_add`) and inversion-of-negation `(σ^i.val)⁻¹ = σ^(-i).val` (`spow_neg`) follow from `ZMod.val_add` and `pow_mod`.

2. **Reflection commutation.** From the single relation τσ = σ⁻¹τ, an induction on m gives `σ^m·τ = τ·(σ^m)⁻¹` (`sigma_pow_mul_tau`). This is the only place the τ-relation is used.

3. **Combination laws.** `rot_mul_refl` and `refl_mul_refl` combine steps 1–2 to compute `σ^i·(τ·σ^j)` and `(τ·σ^i)·(τ·σ^j)`, the two mixed products; the τ² = 1 relation makes the two reflections cancel in `refl_mul_refl`.

4. **The lift.** `liftHom` has `map_one'` immediate and `map_mul'` a four-case match on `DihedralGroup n`'s constructors (r·r, r·sr, sr·r, sr·sr), each discharged by a Mathlib multiplication simp lemma followed by the corresponding law from steps 1–3. Crucially none of this is a finite `decide`, so it holds for an arbitrary carrier G.

5. **Recognition.** With `[Finite G]`: surjectivity of `liftHom` follows from generation (its range contains σ = liftHom(r 1) and τ = liftHom(sr 0), hence ⊤); then `Fintype.card (DihedralGroup n) = 2n = Nat.card G` upgrades surjectivity to bijectivity via `Fintype.bijective_iff_surjective_and_card`, and `MulEquiv.ofBijective … |>.symm` delivers `G ≃* DihedralGroup n`.
keyInsights: **The parent's Sylow route does not generalise; the generators-and-relations route does.** The order-8-subgroup-of-S₄ argument works only because 8 is the full 2-part of |S₄|. The reusable, n-uniform core is instead `DihedralGroup.lift`: build a homomorphism OUT of `DihedralGroup n` by pattern-matching on its constructors and proving `map_mul` from the relations, then upgrade to a MulEquiv by matching orders.

**Proving the homomorphism law for an arbitrary carrier G — not a finite S_k — is exactly what makes the tool reusable, and it needs only two facts:** the ZMod-periodicity lemma σ^(k % n) = σ^k (from σⁿ = 1) and the single commutation identity σ^m·τ = τ·(σ^m)⁻¹ (from τσ = σ⁻¹τ). Every one of the four DihedralGroup multiplication cases reduces to these two. This is why the proof avoids `decide` and therefore avoids any finiteness assumption on G at the homomorphism stage.

**For recognition (not just a homomorphism) the cheap sufficient hypotheses are generation plus an order match.** Generation `closure {σ, τ} = ⊤` gives surjectivity for free, since `liftHom` already hits both generators (σ = liftHom(r 1), τ = liftHom(sr 0)); and |G| = 2n = |DihedralGroup n| gives injectivity for free via `Fintype.bijective_iff_surjective_and_card`. No hand-verification of injectivity — no kernel computation — is needed.

**The reflection relation τ² = 1 is used in exactly one place:** it is what lets the two reflections cancel in `refl_mul_refl`, turning (τσ^i)(τσ^j) into a pure rotation σ^(j-i). Isolating this makes the dependency structure of the dihedral relations transparent: σⁿ = 1 governs the rotation half, τσ = σ⁻¹τ governs commutation, and τ² = 1 governs reflection composition.

**This is a self-contained, upstream-contributable Mathlib addition.** The lift and recognition theorem mention no field theory whatsoever; they belong in `Mathlib.GroupTheory.SpecificGroups.Dihedral` alongside `DihedralGroup.card`, and would serve any formalisation — Galois-theoretic or otherwise — that needs to identify a concretely-presented order-2n group as D_n.

sections.summary: Imports (single Mathlib umbrella) and the top-level docstring: the parent OQ 'general criterion for Gal(X^n − a / ℚ) dihedral?', why the parent's n=4 Sylow route does not generalise, the concrete Mathlib gap (`DihedralGroup.lift` is absent from v4.26.0), and the two Capelli-free deliverables — `liftHom` and `nonempty_mulEquiv_dihedralGroup`. Sets up the variable context `{G} [Group G] {n : ℕ} {σ τ : G}`.
sections.mathContext: General (n, a) dihedral criterion blocked upstream on Capelli; this file isolates the pure group-theoretic core that is provable now.

sections.title: §1: Well-definedness of σ-powers modulo n (pow_mod, spow_add, spow_neg)
sections.summary: The rotation half. `pow_mod`: σ^(k % n) = σ^k from σⁿ = 1. `spow_add`: `i ↦ σ^i.val` is additive on ZMod n. `spow_neg`: it sends negation to inversion. Together these make the rotation map a well-defined additive ZMod n → G map.
sections.mathContext: σⁿ = 1 ⟹ σ^k depends only on k mod n; the rotation map ZMod n → G, i ↦ σ^{i.val}, is an additive homomorphism.

sections.title: §2: The reflection–rotation commutation law (sigma_pow_mul_tau)
sections.summary: `sigma_pow_mul_tau : σ^m · τ = τ · (σ^m)⁻¹`, proved by induction on m from the single relation τσ = σ⁻¹τ. The engine that lets `map_mul'` handle every mixed rotation/reflection product.
sections.mathContext: From tσ = σ⁻¹t: by induction σ^m·t = t·(σ^m)⁻¹ — the reflection conjugates each rotation power to its inverse.

sections.title: §3: Combination laws (rot_mul_refl, refl_mul_refl)
sections.summary: `rot_mul_refl`: σ^i·(τ·σ^j) = τ·σ^(j-i). `refl_mul_refl`: (τ·σ^i)·(τ·σ^j) = σ^(j-i), where τ² = 1 cancels the two reflections. The two mixed-product identities feeding `map_mul'`.
sections.mathContext: The Cayley products of rotations and reflections, written in the normal form τ^ε σ^k.

sections.title: §4: The dihedral lift (liftFun, liftHom, simp lemmas)
sections.summary: `liftFun` (r i ↦ σ^i.val, sr i ↦ τ·σ^i.val) and `liftHom : DihedralGroup n →* G`, the missing `DihedralGroup.lift`. `map_one'` is immediate; `map_mul'` is the four-case constructor match (r·r, r·sr, sr·r, sr·sr), each discharged by a DihedralGroup simp lemma plus a §1–§3 law — no `decide`, so it holds for arbitrary G. The `@[simp]` lemmas `liftHom_r_one : liftHom (r 1) = σ` and `liftHom_sr_zero : liftHom (sr 0) = τ` pin the images of the two generators.
sections.mathContext: The homomorphism D_n → G determined on generators by r 1 ↦ σ, sr 0 ↦ τ, well-defined because σ, τ satisfy the defining relations.

sections.title: §5: The dihedral recognition theorem (nonempty_mulEquiv_dihedralGroup)
sections.summary: `nonempty_mulEquiv_dihedralGroup`: for finite G with the dihedral relations, generation `closure {σ, τ} = ⊤`, and `Nat.card G = 2n` (n ≥ 2), `G ≃* DihedralGroup n`. Surjectivity of `liftHom` from generation (range ⊇ {σ, τ} = ⊤ via the simp lemmas); bijectivity from the card match `Fintype.card (DihedralGroup n) = 2n = Nat.card G` through `Fintype.bijective_iff_surjective_and_card`; `MulEquiv.ofBijective … |>.symm` finishes.
sections.mathContext: A finite group generated by a rotation/reflection pair obeying the dihedral relations, of order 2n, is D_n — the n-uniform recognition criterion replacing the parent's Sylow argument.

conclusion.summary: The reusable group-theoretic core of the general dihedral-binomial problem is now fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, 0 `native_decide`): `liftHom` supplies the `DihedralGroup.lift` that Mathlib v4.26.0 lacks — a homomorphism `DihedralGroup n →* G` built from a generator pair satisfying σⁿ = 1, τ² = 1, τσ = σ⁻¹τ, with the homomorphism law proved from the relations (not by `decide`, so valid for any carrier G) — and `nonempty_mulEquiv_dihedralGroup` upgrades this, under generation and an order match |G| = 2n, to a recognition theorem G ≃* DihedralGroup n.
conclusion.implications: This is the n-uniform replacement for the parent oq-03's n=4-specific Sylow argument: any Galois group Gal(X^n − a / ℚ) exhibited with two generators obeying the dihedral relations and of order 2n is identified as D_n with no further group-theoretic work. The result is entirely field-theory-free and directly upstream-contributable to `Mathlib.GroupTheory.SpecificGroups.Dihedral`.
openQuestions: **Feed the recognition theorem a second concrete case.** Exhibit explicit generators σ, τ for a non-n=4 dihedral binomial (e.g. Gal(X³ − 2 / ℚ) ≅ S₃ ≅ D₃) and apply `nonempty_mulEquiv_dihedralGroup` to obtain the isomorphism.
**Re-derive the parent (4, 2) case through recognition.** Once explicit generators of Gal(X⁴ − 2 / ℚ) are named, `nonempty_mulEquiv_dihedralGroup` gives an alternative to the Sylow route.
**Upstream the lift.** Polish `liftHom` / `nonempty_mulEquiv_dihedralGroup` into a Mathlib PR adding `DihedralGroup.lift`.
**The remaining upstream blocker is Capelli's irreducibility theorem**, needed for the full Schinzel–Velez criterion over arbitrary (n, a); it is independent of this group-theoretic core.

mainTheorems.name: liftHom
mainTheorems.statement: [NeZero n] → σ ^ n = 1 → τ ^ 2 = 1 → τ * σ = σ⁻¹ * τ → DihedralGroup n →* G
mainTheorems.description: The missing `DihedralGroup.lift`: the canonical group homomorphism `DihedralGroup n →* G` induced by generators σ, τ satisfying the dihedral relations. Sends the abstract rotation `r 1` to σ and the abstract reflection `sr 0` to τ. `map_mul'` is proved by a four-case match on `DihedralGroup n`'s constructors, each reduced to periodicity (`spow_add`) and the reflection commutation law (`sigma_pow_mul_tau`) — no finite `decide`, so it applies to an arbitrary carrier group G.
mainTheorems.significance: The reusable presentation-by-generators-and-relations constructor absent from Mathlib v4.26.0; the group-theoretic core every dihedral-binomial case needs.

mainTheorems.name: nonempty_mulEquiv_dihedralGroup
mainTheorems.statement: [Finite G] → 2 ≤ n → σ ^ n = 1 → τ ^ 2 = 1 → τ * σ = σ⁻¹ * τ → Subgroup.closure {σ, τ} = ⊤ → Nat.card G = 2 * n → Nonempty (G ≃* DihedralGroup n)
mainTheorems.description: The dihedral RECOGNITION theorem: a finite group G generated by σ, τ satisfying the dihedral relations, of order 2n (n ≥ 2), is isomorphic to DihedralGroup n. Proof: `liftHom` is surjective because its range contains both generators (σ = liftHom(r 1), τ = liftHom(sr 0)) hence equals ⊤; the cardinality match Fintype.card (DihedralGroup n) = 2n = Nat.card G upgrades surjectivity to bijectivity via `Fintype.bijective_iff_surjective_and_card`; `MulEquiv.ofBijective … |>.symm` yields the isomorphism.
mainTheorems.significance: The n-uniform replacement for the parent oq-03's n=4-specific Sylow argument — identifies any suitably-generated order-2n group as D_n with no further work.

mainTheorems.name: sigma_pow_mul_tau
mainTheorems.statement: τ * σ = σ⁻¹ * τ → ∀ m, σ ^ m * τ = τ * (σ ^ m)⁻¹
mainTheorems.description: The iterated reflection–rotation commutation law, proved by induction on m from the single relation τσ = σ⁻¹τ. The reflection conjugates each rotation power to its inverse.
mainTheorems.significance: The engine behind `liftHom`'s `map_mul'`: every mixed rotation/reflection product in the four DihedralGroup cases reduces to this identity plus periodicity.

mainTheorems.name: pow_mod
mainTheorems.statement: σ ^ n = 1 → ∀ k, σ ^ (k % n) = σ ^ k
mainTheorems.description: σ-powers are periodic with period n once σⁿ = 1 — proved by writing k = (k / n)·n + k % n and collapsing the σⁿ = 1 factor. Makes the rotation map `i ↦ σ^i.val` well-defined modulo n.
mainTheorems.significance: The well-definedness bridge underpinning `spow_add`, `spow_neg`, and hence the entire rotation half of the lift.

mainTheorems.name: refl_mul_refl
mainTheorems.statement: [NeZero n] → σ ^ n = 1 → τ ^ 2 = 1 → τ * σ = σ⁻¹ * τ → ∀ i j : ZMod n, (τ * σ ^ i.val) * (τ * σ ^ j.val) = σ ^ (j - i).val
mainTheorems.description: Reflection-times-reflection combination law: the product of two reflections is a pure rotation σ^(j-i), where the relation τ² = 1 cancels the two τ's. The single place the reflection relation τ² = 1 is used.
mainTheorems.significance: The sr·sr case of `map_mul'`; isolates the role of τ² = 1 in the dihedral relation set.
